In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods for the purification and characterization of the protoxin of Bacillus thuringensis subsp. kurtsaki HD-73, the most effective commercial insecticide.
the chemical modification of the protoxin from Bacillius thuringiensis HD-73, a protein which is used commercially to control insect populations.
the development of new methods of solubilizing the crystal protein from Bacillus thurinigiensis subsp kurstaki HD73.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crystal protein of Bacillus thuringensis is a highly stable protein, which can be modified at the cysteine or lysine residues without affecting the conformation of its native state.
the solubilization of Bt protoxin is a complex phenomenon involving both the cysteine (and perhaps the lysine) residues and the conformation of Bt protoxins.
the solubility of B. thuringiensis protoxin can be increased by chemical modification of cysteine and/or lysine residues, but the increase is only significant for cysteine residues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(a) the cysteine residue(s) are essential for solubilizing protoxin at neutral pH values; (b) modification of lysine residues also enhances the solubility; and (c) the insecticidal activity is not significantly altered by chemical derivatization of cysteine or lysine residues.
all the 16 cysteines and modified lysines are on the surface.
the protoxin is a very stable protein with a very low number of accessible surface amino groups and carboxyl groups.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the solubility of the native crystal protein is a function of the number of ionic groups at the surface.
the solubilities of the B. thuringiensis protoxin and its cysteine and carboxylate derivatives can be significantly enhanced by the addition of a small number of succinyl groups.
derivatization of the surface cysteine and modified lysine residue(s) does not alter the structure or function of the protoxin.
